condition_spec.note: `effort-low` on Grok 4.7. Same overlay and effort as `effort-low`. The process is `grok -p`, so the tool names differ and there is no dollar cap (Grok has no `--max-budget-usd`). The turn cap matches the set.

argv:
Several problems around closing, reopening and overdue issues:

1. The project card counts canceled issues as open. Done and canceled issues are both closed; every other status is open.
2. The project card's overdue count includes issues that are already done or canceled. Only open, non-archived issues whose due time has passed count as overdue.
3. An issue that is reopened (moved from done or canceled back to an open status) still shows a completion date. Reopening must clear the completion date, and closing again sets a new one. The start date stays the first time the issue went in progress.
4. The periodic overdue sweep (the job that announces overdue issues, which in turn alerts their assignees) announces canceled issues. It must announce only open, non-archived issues whose due time has passed; an issue due exactly at the time of the sweep is not overdue yet.
5. The sweep never covers brand-new workspaces, so their members get no overdue alerts at all, while it still covers workspaces that have been deleted. It must cover every workspace that has not been deleted, and no deleted one.
6. Once the sweep has announced an issue, it never announces it again for as long as the server runs, even after the issue was canceled and reopened while still past due, or its due date was moved out and then passed again. The rule: the first sweep that finds an issue overdue announces it; later sweeps do not announce it again as long as every sweep in between also found it overdue; once a sweep finds it not overdue (closed, archived, or due in the future), the next sweep that finds it overdue again announces it again.
7. Overdue alerts are filed under the wrong kind of notification: they show up under "due soon" in the inbox filter, people who switched off overdue alerts in their notification settings still get them, and people who switched off "due soon" alerts stop getting overdue alerts. Overdue alerts must be filed as overdue alerts and follow only the overdue-alert setting. Alerts stay within their own workspace.
